# New renderings chosen in iliad-077 (Iliad 13.1–80)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ἱππόπολος (ἱπποπόλων Θρῃκῶν, 13.4) | "horse-herding" | "horse-herding" | "horse-breeding", "horse-rearing", "horse-taming" (reserved for ἱππόδαμος); the second half is taken as "tending", the note says so |
| ἀγχέμαχος (Μυσῶν ἀγχεμάχων, 13.5) | "close-fighting" | "close-fighting" | "fighting hand to hand", "spear-fighting"; follows the table’s ἀγχιμαχητής "close-fighters" |
| ἱππημολγός · γλακτοφάγος (ἀγαυῶν ἱππημολγῶν γλακτοφάγων, 13.5–6) | "mare-milkers" · "milk-eaters" | "mare-milkers" · "the milk-eaters" | "milk-drinkers", "mare-milking"; the English leaves open whether these two words and the Abii are one people or two, as the Greek does |
| Σάμος Θρηϊκίη (Σάμου ὑληέσσης Θρηϊκίης, 13.12–13) | "wooded Samos, the Thracian" | "wooded Thracian Samos" | "Samothrace" (the later name; the note gives it); ὑληέσσης "wooded" as the table’s ὑληέσσῃ (6.396) |
| κραιπνὰ ποσὶ προβιβάς (13.18) | "at a rush with his feet, striding forward" | "striding forward at a rush on his feet" | not new: the Odyssey’s same words (17.27) "at a rush … striding forward" / "striding forward at a rush", with ποσί added; "swiftly" (reserved for ὠκύς, θοός), "rapidly", "in a rush" |
| τέκμωρ (τὸ δὲ τέτρατον ἵκετο τέκμωρ, 13.20) | "reached the end" | "reached his journey’s end" | "sign" (the Iliad’s rendering where the word is a pledge given; here it is the goal reached, as in the Odyssey’s "end"), "goal" |
| λίμνη (βένθεσι λίμνης, 13.21; βαθείης … λίμνης, 13.32) | "the depths of the water" · "the deep water" | same | "lake", "pool" (a lake is not meant), "sea" (the note says λίμνη is standing or open water, here the sea); follows the Odyssey’s ἀνεδύσετο λίμνης "rose up from the water" |
| ὀρέγω (τρὶς … ὀρέξατ’, 13.20) | "stretched himself" | "strode out" | "reached", "stepped"; the Greek does not name the stride, the note says so |
| ἄταλλε κήτε’ (13.27) | "frolicked" · "sea-monsters" | "came frolicking" · "sea-monsters" | "gambolled", "played"; "whales", "sea-beasts"; κῆτος "sea-monster" as the Odyssey’s μεγακήτεϊ |
| ἠγνοίησεν (οὐδ’ ἠγνοίησεν ἄνακτα, 13.28) | "did not fail to recognize" | "did not fail to know" | not new: the table’s ἠγνοίησεν ἰδοῦσ’ (1.536–537), double negative kept; "did not mistake", "recognised at once"; ἄναξ "lord" (table) |
| κευθμῶν (ἐκ κευθμῶν, 13.28) | "hiding-places" | "recesses" | not new: the table’s κευθμῶν row, same English in both layers as there |
| γηθοσύνῃ δὲ θάλασσα διίστατο (13.29) | "and for joy the sea parted" | "and the sea parted for joy" | "stood apart", "drew back", "with gladness" |
| ῥίμφα μάλ’ (13.30) | "very nimbly" | "very nimbly" | "lightly" (the table keeps it for Paris running, 6.511), "swiftly"; the table’s ῥίμφα "nimbly" (8.54) with μάλα "very" |
| ἐΰσκαρθμος (13.31, of horses) | "well-bounding" | "well-bounding" | "springing", "swift-leaping", "nimble-footed"; ἐΰ "well", σκαρθμός "leap"; the note says the formation is not certain |
| πέδη (πέδας … χρυσείας, 13.36) | "fetters" | "fetters" | "shackles", "hobbles", "chains", "bonds" (kept for δεσμοί) |
| ἀρρήκτους ἀλύτους, ὄφρ’ ἔμπεδον αὖθι μένοιεν (13.37) | "unbreakable, not to be undone, so that firmly on the spot they would stay" | "that could not be broken or undone, so that they would stay fast right there" | not new: the Odyssey’s same line (odyssey-035, 8.275), reused; the object changed from δεσμούς to πέδας, so `i` opens "that could not be broken or undone" |
| μένοιεν νοστήσαντα ἄνακτα (13.37–38) | "stay for their lord, having returned" | "stay fast right there until their lord came back" | "wait for" in `l`, "await"; μένω takes the accusative of the one waited for, the note says so |
| ἄβρομοι αὐΐαχοι (13.41) | "roaring, shouting" | "roaring and shouting" | "clamorous", "loud-shouting", "boisterous"; the sense of both words is not secure and the note says so (ἄβρομος taken from βρόμος "roar") |
| εἰσάμενος Κάλχαντι δέμας καὶ ἀτειρέα φωνήν (13.45) | "making himself like Calchas in body and in unwearied voice" | "taking the likeness of Calchas in body and in his unwearied voice" | "disguised as", "in the guise of"; follows the table’s εἰσάμενος "took the likeness of …" and ἀτειρής "unwearied" |
| Αἴαντε πρώτω προσέφη μεμαῶτε καὶ αὐτώ (13.46) | "The two Ajaxes first he addressed, both eager, of themselves too:" | "He spoke to the two Ajaxes first, both of them eager of their own accord:" | "To the two Ajaxes he said first"; the duals kept ("the two Ajaxes", as the table’s Αἴαντε δύω), καὶ αὐτώ taken as "of their own accord" |
| κρυεροῖο φόβοιο (13.48) | "chilling flight" | "chilling flight" | "icy", "cold"; follows the table’s κρυερὸς γόος "chilling lament" and φόβος "flight" |
| ἄλλῃ μέν … τῇ δὲ δή (13.49, 13.52) | "For elsewhere" … "But there indeed" | "For elsewhere" … "But there" | "on one side … on the other"; the μέν … δέ pair carried by "elsewhere" / "there" |
| ἕξουσιν … πάντας (13.51) | "will hold" | "will hold … back" | "will withstand", "will keep off"; ἔχω "hold" in the sense "hold in check", the note says so |
| αἰνότατον (13.52, adverb) | "most dreadfully" | "most dreadfully" | "most terribly", "most fearfully"; αἰνός "dread" as the table’s αἰνότατε "most dread" |
| εὔχετ’ … εἶναι (13.54) | "boasts to be" | "claims to be" | "prays to be", "vaunts that he is" |
| ἐνὶ φρεσὶ ποιήσειεν (13.55) | "in your wits put it" | "put it in the minds of you two" | "grant you", "inspire you"; φρένες "wits" in `l`, "minds" in `i` |
| ἀνωγέμεν ἄλλους (13.56) | "to bid the others" | "to bid the others do the same" | "to urge on" (reserved for ὀτρύνω); ἄνωγα "bid" as in the table; the thing bidden is understood and said so in the note |
| ἐρωήσαιτ’ (13.57) | "drive back" | "drive back" | "check", "repel", "turn back"; ἐρωέω "draw back", transitive here |
| ἦ καί (13.59) | "He spoke, and" | "So he said, and" | not new: the table’s ἦ καί (1.219, 14.494); "So he spoke" is reserved for ὣς φάτο / ὣς ἔφατο |
| σκηπάνιον (13.59) | "staff" | "his staff" | "sceptre" (reserved for σκῆπτρον), "wand", "rod"; a rare word, the note says so |
| μένος κρατερόν (μένεος κρατεροῖο, 13.60) | "strong fury" | "strong fury" | "mighty might", "strong strength"; μένος "fury" (the table keeps it clear of the wrath-words), κρατερός "strong" |
| πόδας καὶ χεῖρας ὕπερθεν (13.61; ἔνερθε / ὕπερθε, 13.75) | "the feet below and the hands above" | "their feet below and their hands above" | "feet and hands alike"; ὕπερθεν "above" goes with the hands, "below" is taken from ἔνερθε at 13.75 and the note says so |
| αἰγίλιψ πέτρη (13.63) | "sheer rock" | "a sheer … rock" | "goat-forsaken", "goat-shunned", "steep" (each silently picks a guess); the meaning is not known, "sheer" is the guess, and the note says so |
| περιμήκης (13.63) | "very tall" | "very tall" | "very long", "tall"; περι- "very" as in περικαλλής "very fair" |
| Αἴαντα … Τελαμώνιον υἱόν (13.67) | "Ajax … the Telamonian son" | "Ajax, Telamon’s son" | "Ajax son of Telamon"; the table’s Τελαμώνιον υἱόν "great Telamonian son" / "Telamon’s great son" with μέγας dropped |
| ἐφορμᾶται πολεμίζειν (13.74) | "is impelled to wage war and to fight" | "is impelled to wage war and to fight" | "is eager to" (reserved for μεμαώς), "rushes upon" (the table’s ἐφορμάομαι is for a physical rush), "is set on" |
| στήθεσσι φίλοισι (13.73) | "within my dear chest" | "in my own chest" | "my dear breast", "my beloved chest"; φίλος with a part of the body is little more than "own", the note says so; στῆθος "chest" as the table’s στήθεσσιν λασίοισι |
| μαιμώωσι · μαιμῶσιν (13.75, 13.78) | "rage" | "are raging" | "are eager" (reserved for μεμαώς), "quiver"; the table’s μαιμάω "be eager, rage", "raging" / "raged", same English at both places |
| μένος ὤρορε (13.78) | "has been roused" | "has been roused" | "has risen" (the subject is not stated), "has stirred"; ὄρνυμι "rouse"; the English leaves the subject unsaid, as the Greek does |
| ἔσσυμαι (13.79) | "I am hurrying" | "I am hurrying" | "I am rushing" (kept for κραιπνά "at a rush"), "I am eager" (reserved for μεμαώς); the table’s ἐσσύμενον "hurrying" |
| μενοινώω (13.79) | "I yearn" | "I yearn" | "I am eager" (reserved for μεμαώς), "I long", "I desire" |
| ἔνθ’ ἐλθὼν ὑπ’ ὄχεσφι τιτύσκετο χαλκόποδ’ ἵππω … (13.23–24; the second line is also 8.42, iliad-046) | "There, having come, under the chariot he was making ready two bronze-footed horses, / swift-flying, with golden manes worn long," | "There he came and harnessed to his chariot his two bronze-hoofed horses, swift of flight, with their long golden manes," | "yoked", "bronze-shod"; the published unit (8.41–42) begins ὣς εἰπών, so this unit is new, but the wording of the horses is the published one |
